question: Should OpenClaw admit operator-configured `workspace-directory` Codex plugins only when the exact catalog ID is already installed and enabled, `plugin/read` proves owned app IDs, and `app/list` proves current accessibility, with no OpenClaw installation authority?
rationale: The implementation can enforce the proposed constraints, but deciding whether account-scoped plugin capabilities belong inside OpenClaw's native Codex trust boundary requires maintainer intent; the earlier marketplace expansion and revert confirm this is deliberate policy.

options.title: Approve constrained workspace support
options.body: Accept exact-ID, already-active, ownership-verified, app-accessible workspace plugins and fail closed on incompatible servers.

options.title: Retain curated-only support
options.body: Reject workspace-directory admission and keep the current native plugin trust boundary unchanged.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained workspace support
recommendation.body: Accept exact-ID, already-active, ownership-verified, app-accessible workspace plugins and fail closed on incompatible servers.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and materially contributed to the prior marketplace expansion, providing the strongest available decision-routing signal beyond the current contributor.
